policy_title: Reduce Household Costs and Support Families
stated: Labour will take action to support families by tackling the underlying causes of the cost-of-living crisis: reducing energy costs, lowering food prices by removing trade barriers, making housing more affordable, expanding childcare access, and ensuring work pays. They will introduce free breakfast clubs in every primary school, keep mortgage rates low via an independent Bank of England, and commit to no increases in National Insurance, Income Tax (basic, higher, or additional rates), or VAT.

source.quote: Labour will take action to support families, by tackling the underlying causes of the crisis. We will bring down the cost of energy. We will reduce food prices by removing barriers to businesses trading. We will make housing more affordable, expand access to childcare, and make work pay. We will support families with children by introducing free breakfast clubs in every primary school. Labour will also keep mortgage rates as low as possible, with a strong, independent Bank of England – which will continue to target stable inflation of 2 per cent. We will ensure taxes on working people are kept as low as possible. Labour will not increase taxes on working people, which is why we will not increase National Insurance, the basic, higher, or additional rates of Income Tax, or VAT.

bearing_set.reason: Multiple direct mechanisms — reducing energy costs, lowering food prices via trade barriers, free breakfast clubs (reducing food expenditure per household), and an explicit commitment to no rises in NI, Income Tax, or VAT — all bear materially on real disposable income and essential-cost indicators.

Explicitly commits to 'making housing more affordable' and to keeping mortgage rates low via an independent Bank of England; both directly affect the house-price-to-income ratio and mortgage affordability indicators.

Free breakfast clubs in every primary school and expanded childcare access are direct early-years and education-opportunity interventions that earn a real verdict on attainment, the attainment gap, and access indicators.

Childcare expansion is a well-evidenced lever for labour-market participation (especially for mothers), and the explicit commitment to 'ensuring work pays' targets in-work poverty — together earning a real verdict on job quality and take-home pay indicators.
Explicit commitments to no increases in National Insurance, Income Tax (all rates), or VAT directly bear on household tax burden and take-home pay.

Specific new spending pledges (breakfast clubs, childcare expansion) alongside a hard no-tax-increase commitment creates a concrete funding-gap mechanism that could widen the deficit or require borrowing, bearing on debt-path sustainability.

membership_note: Broad multi-strand package; five fundamentals all earn genuine verdicts. 'Ensuring work pays' is stated but without a concrete pay or rights mechanism, so O4 does not clear the non-negligible bar. Inequality (O14) effects are plausibly progressive but derivative of the O2 and O7 channels rather than independently scored.
